industry.key: K. Professional, business and consumer services
industry.why: Neutral, carried unchanged by judgement; see component 1, Special topics, Topic 1 (Recruitment Services). Component 1 regime, 2-Oct-26 (rates-led late cycle, hiking path marked down for the first time this week, growth firm at the level and rolling at the margin, index calm with risk-off running beneath it through breadth, size and rate sensitivity, not through defensives; sources present 2026-W40): the industry's composite rank (66, from 20 on 3-Jul) is a relief rally in the artificial-intelligence-exposed labour-service names measured by a composite weighted to the last six months, with the twelve-month return still -6.94% against the index; the seven sectors are split (Recruitment D, Advertising C, Testing B, the rest C) and the sector rows carry the view. Relative strength C now, C prior. Counter-case: if the recruiters' rebound is the early-cycle hiring turn, this industry leads and C is late.

sector.why: Neutral, from Underweight; see component 1, Special topics, Topic 1 (Recruitment Services), which carries the same letter. Component 1 regime, 2-Oct-26 (rates-led late cycle, hiking path marked down for the first time this week, growth firm at the level and rolling at the margin, index calm with risk-off running beneath it through breadth, size and rate sensitivity, not through defensives; sources present 2026-W40): the sector rose with the same artificial-intelligence-fear reversal as the recruiters (WPP +56.6%, JCDecaux +27.9% from 1-Jul to 1-Oct) but its footing is firmer: twelve-month relative return +3.1%, rank 83 reached in July and held, sell-side momentum B for WPP and JCDecaux, and the 'first budget cut' case that set D has not appeared in the growth data (US GDP +3.4%, euro area expanding). Relative strength B now, C prior, agrees on direction. Counter-case: advertising is still the first discretionary corporate spend cut when the margin rolls over, and the consumer-agent theme threatens the brands that buy it; balanced, so Neutral.

geography.why: Double Underweight, carried. Component 1 regime, 30-Oct-26 (risk-off beneath a steady index, led now by credit and the cost of debt rather than by the artificial intelligence wash-out alone: the US ten-year above 5% after a hawkish Fed hold with two dissents for a hike, Goldman Sachs' Risk Appetite Indicator at its lowest since April 2025, euro investment-grade and high-yield yields up 30 and 90 basis points since September, Brent near $115, the French premium a record 150 basis points, Europe rotating to quality, defensives and non-AI growth, the STOXX Europe 600 1.7% from its high with breadth recovering from the bottom fifth of three years and defensives leading cyclicals at four weeks and three months; sources present 2026-W44): the French ten-year premium reached a record 150 basis points, 'a lot for a core European country' (Pacific, 26 October), the 2027 deficit is seen at 5.4% of output (Goldman Sachs, 25 October), euro-exposed assets underperformed their global betas because of France (GOAL, 26 October), 2027's 300 billion of issuance makes this 'just the warmup' and the election in May or June 2027 is the earliest point anything changes; against it, Moody's affirmation removed a sovereign tail risk (DNB Carnegie, 26 October) and the French Hidden Champions newsletter sees institutional outflows from French small and mid caps as a contrarian set-up. Ten Pool names, TotalEnergies at rank 24 near the Bench cut with a global revenue base the row does not describe well. Counter-case: the affirmation and the contrarian set-up. To D on the premium under 120 basis points for a month; back to C under 100.
